item.title: Kratom and 7-OH can feel like 'a miracle.' They can also be addictive
item.description: In the last decade, strong support for kratom and 7-OH products have kept them federally legal. That's started to change. A crackdown for some highly potent products related to kratom is coming.

item.title: Hegseth awards medal to soldier who chastised him
item.description:
Pete Hegseth was yelled at by a sentinel for poor decorum at Arlington National Cemetery. Now the Secretary of Defense has
given him a medal.

item.title: Rivers in the sky are raining down on the Pacific Northwest. What are they?
item.description: Atmospheric rivers are large bands of water vapor in the sky. They are dumping trillions of gallons of water on Washington and Oregon, just as high tides and winds batter shorelines.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Fed up with the healthcare industry, this red state capped insulin prices for patients
item.description: Republicans and Democrats in North Dakota worked together to limit what people with diabetes have to pay for insulin, joining a growing bipartisan push across the country to protect patients.

item.title: Why even a fraction of a degree can escalate climate change impacts
item.description: Countries are not meeting their goal of limiting climate change to 1.5 degrees Celsius. How much hotter the planet gets makes a profound difference for the impacts the world could see.

item.title: Hop in: We're taking a pop culture road trip on Route 66
item.description: Route 66 is celebrating 100 years of being the country's most famous highway. This icon of American culture passes through eight states — and has shown up for decades in movies, books, music and art.
